name: Woodruff Park
story: Robert W. Woodruff, the longtime head of Coca-Cola, quietly bought this land and gave it to the city in 1971. The park opened in 1973 as Central City Park and took his name in 1985, once his gift became known. It is the western start of the trail.

name: APEX Museum
story: Filmmaker Dan Moore Sr. founded the APEX Museum in 1978 to tell history from a Black perspective. It sits in the historic John Wesley Dobbs building and is Atlanta's oldest Black history museum.

name: Sweet Auburn Works
address: Auburn Ave NE near Jesse Hill Jr Dr
story: Sweet Auburn Works is the neighborhood's Main Street organization. It works with business owners, residents and preservation groups to bring new life to the avenue while protecting its history.

name: Municipal Market
story: The market began in 1918 as a farmers' market in a large tent, on land cleared by the Great Atlanta Fire of 1917. Its brick hall opened in 1924. Under segregation, Black shoppers could buy inside, but only white vendors could sell from the indoor stalls. Black vendors sold along the curb outside, one source of the name Curb Market.

name: John Wesley Dobbs Park
address: Auburn Ave NE at Fort St NE
story: John Wesley Dobbs is credited with naming this street Sweet Auburn, and many called him the Mayor of Auburn Avenue. He co-founded the Atlanta Negro Voters League in 1946. The plaza opened in 1996, and its bronze sculpture lets you look out along the avenue through his eyes.

name: Haugabrooks
story: Geneva Haugabrooks, a Spelman College graduate, opened this funeral home in 1929 with three hundred dollars. She built it into a million-dollar business that ran for nearly a century, and her generosity earned her the name Mama Haugabrooks.

name: Ebenezer Church
story: Martin Luther King Jr. was baptized at Ebenezer Baptist Church, and he and his father, Martin Luther King Sr., both served as its pastors. The church stands about a block west of the house where King was born.

name: MLK Center
story: Coretta Scott King founded the King Center in 1968, after her husband's death. Since 1981 it has stood next to Ebenezer Baptist Church. Between the two is the tomb of Dr. and Mrs. King, beside a reflecting pool and an eternal flame.

name: King Birth Home
story: Martin Luther King Jr. was born in this house in 1929. Built in 1895, it was home to his parents after they married in 1926. The surrounding blocks are part of the Martin Luther King Jr. National Historical Park.

name: HDDC
story: The Historic District Development Corporation formed in 1980 to restore this neighborhood. It began with the houses around Dr. King's birth home and has worked outward to bring homes and residents back.

name: Beltline Eastside Trail
story: The trail ends at the Atlanta BeltLine's Eastside Trail. Its first two-mile section opened in October 2012 along an old rail corridor, linking Piedmont Park, the Old Fourth Ward and Inman Park.
